Excellent hike starting at the train station in Ella. Walk along the railroad tracks (there's plenty of time to step off for the occasional train). We had such a lovely time at the bridge! It is a 45 minutes walk over the railway and it is best to check beforehand at what time the train will pass, we did not but were lucky. I don't think anyone will find the idea of walking along train tracks just to look at a bridge "attractive". But if you like exploring the unknown, then this one`s for you! Make sure you enquire to the station master as to when the trains are scheduled, so that you wont be forced to jump off the tracks suddenly when a train approaches from front or behind. The bridge is halfway between Ella and Demodara; it takes about 45 minutes to the bridge from Ella and another 45 minutes from the bridge to Demodara. Distance from Ella to Demodara stations is about 9-10 kms. The walk offers very nice views. I`d recommend to do it early in the morning, so that you don't exhaust yourself- remember Sri Lanka is a tropical country, and it starts getting hot and humid as early as 9.30 or 10 am. Carry water bottle with you because there`s no shop from where you can buy water till Demodara should you need it.  There are leeches on the grass, so wear full length track pants or trousers. Spend some time at the quiet station of Demodara, watch the train from Badulla go below the station around the mountain , and when you board the train back to Ella, make sure you are in the window seat to witness the train actually pass over the bridge- trust me, its worth all the effort!

Asanka the boy with the biggest smile I have ever seen is highly motivated to learn english from tourists and his dream is to build a small hut were he can offer tea for tourists. Having been running Health and Safety projects for some years, I took great pleasure in jumping onto the railway track and heading down it with great abandon. That pleasure turned into mild panic as I hit a tunnel knowing that the 15.30 train was minutes behind me and I needed to get through it if I wanted to get a photo of the train crossing the bridge. Nothing to do but run across the 30 or so meters making every effort not to trip over the sleepers. Got through without any issues with enough time to settle down on the wall of the bridge and wait for the train: got a great photo as the giant engine pulled centimetres past me, passengers waving hello. The scenery as you walk the tracks is as great as anything you will have seen in the hill country. As the bridge finishes you can take the path that climbs steeply upwards and follow it to a road, cross that road and walk through the tea plantation to get to the foot of Little Adam's rock.

If you want to take a look at this place walk along the tracks to get there. We went in a taxi and it struggled with the rough track, eventually not being able to get up a steep slope, so you will need to walk a little way anyway.

Do like Johnny Cash and Walk the Line. Literally. Walking along the railway line from Ella to Demodara is easy, fun, and there is actually a lot to see. And you can't get lost! About half way between the 2 railway stations there are a number of small waterfalls and water pipes next to the railway which deliver crystal clear and cool water. Great for splashing around a bit and freshing up on a hot day! You will meet lots of people walking like yourselves on the railway tracks, from one hamlet to another. Some are curious about the unexpected visitors, some will test their English on you. Some are chatty, some are shy. And they all will point you to Demodara and its famous loop in the tunnel and the bridge. There is a short stretch which actually feels like "jungle" - of course it is not, but stop for a while and listen to the sounds. You will hear and see birds, maybe spotted deer. "Are there leopards in the jungle?" It is not dangerous to walk on the tracks. Trains are slow and noisy. Even in the tunnels (I think there are two to cross) you will have time enough to get out of their way. And like everybody else you will stand there and wave to the train. (When did you do that at home last time?) The walk took us about 1 1/2 hours including lots of stops. We did a bit of calculation, arrived in time to see the train coming, the bridge, the loop, then boarded it in Demodara and rode back to Ella. We felt Extremely Satisfied with our heroic achievement to have walked this far!!! I think the ticket was something like 15 rupees. Ridiculous cheap for a half- day excursion with a lot of fun. Walk the Line!

This bridge between Ella and Demodara was built during the British Era. When one stands under this 99.6ft high bridge and looks up, there is a beautiful sight of 'nine skies' through the nine arches. It is also called 'The Bridge in the sky' due to the sheer hight. Its built entirely of rocks, bricks and cement without any steel. The best view of the bridge, if not on the train journey itself, is on the Ella Passara Road.
